correctness.rationale: Weighted RMS-AM yields N_T(f)>=||f||_1, and pointwise ℓ2<=ℓ1 yields upper S||f||_1. On period-m invariant component, residue aggregation gives b_mr, and a Borel selector E_m of one representative per finite orbit attains Σ_r sqrt(b_mr) by one-marker disjointness. If long orbits exist in positive measure for every L, a countable-cylinder separation of successive orbit points produces positive-measure marker E whose shifts are disjoint on any fixed finite window; their coordinate contributions give lower bound Σ_{k∈F}√a_k, tending to S. Strict positivity ensures S_m<S because each congruence class has several weights and sqrt is strictly subadditive. Equality with S would force all shifted positive-measure supports pairwise disjoint, impossible in a probability space. Pairwise ℓ1−ℓ2 deficit obeys (2−√2)∫min(c_k,c_l)≤S||f||1−N_T(f) and a finite-window upper bound by Σpairs∫min + ||f||1 Σk∉F√a_k; these establish the iff near-extremizer criterion for normalized f. Independent cyclic numerical checks of a_k=(3/5)4^(-|k|) confirmed S=3sqrt(3/5), S1=1, S2=(sqrt(17)+sqrt8)/5, and S_m<S for 1<=m<=19. These are illustrative, not a substitute for orbit-marker proof.
residual_risks: Finite independent enumerations/numerical examples only corroborate explicitly identified analytic or exhaustive-finite arguments; they do not prove unbounded statements.
